tier_reason: The jumprope-rs README table (Ryzen 5800X, single core) shows librope (C) at 16.28/3.93/1.59/10.01 ms vs Raw string 3908.13/569.44/41.05/1238.44 ms, exactly as claimed; it is first-party (author's own rewrite repo), the harness rope_benches/src/main.rs is public but rustc and C compiler versions are never stated, the C flags are left to the cc crate defaults, and the Raw string row is commented out in the current code, so it falls short of A.

corrections.compiler_and_flags: Not fully stated. rope_benches README says to run `cargo run --release -- --bench` (criterion 0.3); the jumprope-rs workspace release profile sets lto = true and codegen-units = 1; rope.c is compiled by the Rust `cc` crate from rope_benches/build.rs with no explicit flags (so the optimization level comes from cargo's release profile, not stated in the README); librope's own Makefile uses -O2 -Wall -std=c99 but that build is not what the table measured. rustc and C compiler versions are not given.
corrections.caveats: First-party: the table lives in the README of the author's own Rust rewrite (jumprope-rs), where librope is a comparison column, not the subject; the table was last updated in October 2021 (commits 7842779 and 6df4d19) and the full criterion report on home.seph.codes is blocked from this environment (EGRESS_BLOCKED), so it was not opened. The 'Raw string' baseline is the author's own Rust String wrapper (rope_benches/src/edittablestr.rs) that finds the byte offset by scanning char_indices from the start on every edit and grows the string one pushed '\0' at a time, so the 25x-240x gaps mostly measure an O(n) character-offset scan on a flat string, not a tuned memmove-based std::string or C char buffer. The String row is commented out in the current rope_benches/src/main.rs ('This takes a long time to run') and passes a variable (&test_data) that no longer exists, and the realworld group loads traces from a hard-coded /home/seph/src/diamond-types/benchmark_data path, so the table is not reproducible out of the box. The C column ('C-JumpRope' in the code) is a vendored copy of rope.c/rope.h inside rope_benches that differs from librope HEAD (ROPE_MAX_HEIGHT 20 instead of 60, skip_size renamed skip_chars, minor type casts); the algorithm is the same. librope is driven through FFI with a CString allocation per insert, which handicaps it slightly. No libstdc++, libc++ or MSVC STL comparison and no C++ std::string or SGI rope baseline appears anywhere (librope's own test/benchmark.c loops only over the first implementation, librope; the 'c string' and SGI crope rows exist but are skipped). The librope README's 15M ops/s figure links to the blocked home.seph.codes report. Last commit 2021-10-13; the author says the library works but he has moved to Rust and points users to Jumprope, which the same table shows is 2-3x faster.

notes: Numbers match the jumprope-rs README exactly; tier C stands (first-party, compiler versions unstated, baseline row disabled in current code). Shortcomings to record: baseline is a naive Rust String with an O(n) char-offset scan per edit (not std::string or a C buffer), table dates from 2021-10 and is not reproducible as checked in, benchmarked rope.c is a lightly modified vendored copy (ROPE_MAX_HEIGHT 20), and the library is superseded by the author's own 2-3x faster Jumprope. maintenance_status corrected to abandoned (last commit 2021-10-13, about 5 years old; the README says it works but the author moved on, not that it is complete).
